title: C# Introduction
summary: Meet C#, pronounced C sharp. Write a greeting, add two small numbers and make a choice based on a score.
introduction: C# is pronounced C sharp. It is a language for writing apps, games and other programs. It works with a tool kit called .NET. Start with a few short steps: show a message, count pencils and check a score. You can read the code even before you install the tools.
learningObjectives: Print a greeting and add two numbers
Use if to check a score

rows: A language for writing steps a computer can follow.
Tools and ready-made parts used by C# programs.
A name for a value the program remembers.

blocks.title: Where to run the examples
blocks.text: Read the [setup lesson](/tutorials/csharp/setup-dotnet) to use C# on your computer. These examples are shown here for reading; they do not run in this site playground.
Console.WriteLine prints text and starts a new line. Put this code in Program.cs in the console project from the setup lesson.
int means a whole number. Each variable gives a name to a value. The plus sign adds the two numbers.

blocks.title: Program.cs

blocks.text: An if statement asks a yes-or-no question. Here it asks whether the score is at least 5.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.text: C# and C++ are different languages. Use dotnet for these C# examples. Keep the capital letters in Console.WriteLine.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Replace Asha with your name. Then change the score to 3 and predict whether the last message appears.
